t: I'll show you how AI can handle
incoming leads right inside Bitrix,
without a manager sorting every chat.
One of my projects: an online school
that wanted to automate incoming leads.
First, we broke down the process itself.
A person writes in the chat,
messages arrive in Bitrix,
AI gets the context, analyzes the request,
figures out what the person wants,
qualifies the lead, drafts a reply
and then works with the CRM itself.
AI structures the lead data
and writes it back to Bitrix.
So the manager doesn't open every chat
doing the same routine work by hand.
So: where staff repeat one task every day,
where there are clear rules,
where there is input data
and a concrete, measurable result.
These are the processes that most often
become a good entry point for automation.
Good AI in business is part of a process
that should save time,
improve the team's work
and give measurable results.
So don't put AI into everything at once.
Find one process, break it down,
find repetitive, rule-based actions
and automate those first.
Then scale the system.
More architectures and cases on my Telegram.
Nailed it, right?
